title: U.S. House · New York's 15th District
area: The South Bronx, including Concourse, Highbridge, Morrisania, Hunts Point, Soundview, Parkchester, Castle Hill, and Co-op City.

context.text: Incumbent Ritchie Torres won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 58.1% of the vote, defeating Jose Vega (22.2%) and Michael Blake (19.1%).
The Republican primary (Stylo A. Sapaskis) and Conservative Party primary (Gonzalo Duran) were both canceled; each candidate advanced unopposed.
John Maynard Harris, who had been listed under the 'What The H.E.C.' party line, withdrew or was disqualified and does not appear on the November 3 general-election ballot.

summary.text: Torres is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for NY-15, first elected in 2020 after serving on the New York City Council. He sits on the House Financial Services Committee and the Select Committee on Strategic Competition with the Chinese Communist Party, and has sponsored legislation on housing, immigration-detention oversight, and campaign-finance transparency.

background.text: Torres graduated from Herbert H. Lehman High School in the Bronx and attended New York University.
Before seeking office, Torres worked as a staffer to New York City Council member James Vacca, focusing on housing issues.
Torres served on the New York City Council representing District 15 from 2013 to 2021 before his election to Congress.
Torres was a delegate to the 2016 Democratic National Convention.

priorities.text: "Bronx needs one of our own to fight for us in Washington, and I'm honored to carry the mantle."

"I'm fighting for quality health care and housing, schools and jobs. I'm standing up for immigrants, seniors, and youth. I'm fighting everyday to protect our neighborhoods from gun violence and make the Bronx a safe, decent, affordable place to live."

positions.summary: Torres sponsored the Point-Access Housing Guidelines Act of 2025, which directs HUD to issue federal guidelines to help states and localities permit 'point-access' (single-stairwell) apartment buildings, a building-code change intended to make more housing construction feasible; the bill was incorporated into the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which became law.
After Gov. Hochul's 2024 move to indefinitely delay congestion pricing, Torres said the pause would jeopardize the MTA's capital plan and public-health investments promised to the Bronx.
positions.quote: The central concern is not so much congestion pricing as it is the preservation of a public transit system that is too big to fail.

positions.summary: Torres's campaign material says he is working to protect Bronx neighborhoods from gun violence.
positions.quote: I'm fighting everyday to protect our neighborhoods from gun violence and make the Bronx a safe, decent, affordable place to live.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services (Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence; Housing and Insurance; National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions subcommittees) and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, 119th Congress.

Sponsored the Housing Temperature Safety Act of 2025 (H.R. 638), introduced January 22, 2025, which would pilot a program requiring owners of federally subsidized rental units to install heat sensors and would let housing agencies automatically issue violations against non-compliant landlords.

Sponsored the Helping More Families Save Act (H.R. 4385) with Rep. William Timmons, introduced July 14, 2025, to let HUD-assisted families build escrow savings from rising earned income without losing benefit eligibility; provisions from the bill passed the House as part of the Housing for the 21st Century Act.

Sponsored the Point-Access Housing Guidelines Act of 2025 (H.R. 6345), introduced December 1, 2025, directing HUD to issue federal guidelines for permitting point-access ('single-stair') apartment buildings; provisions were incorporated into the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which the President signed into law.

Co-sponsored the Families Deserve to Know Act with Rep. George Latimer (NY-16), introduced August 13, 2026, which would require ICE to notify a detained person's family of a death or medical emergency in custody and to report every custody death to Congress and the public.

candidates.name: Stylo A. Sapaskis
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed after the Republican primary was canceled

summary.text: Sapaskis is a Bronx-based Republican making his third run for NY-15 after losing to Torres in 2022; he has also run for New York City Council and State Senate. His campaign centers on inflation, a higher minimum wage, more police presence, and financial aid for higher education.

background.text: Sapaskis earned an Associate of Applied Science in Corporate Cable Communications from Borough of Manhattan Community College and a Bachelor of Arts in Film Production/Cinema Studies from the City College of New York, and pursued a Master of Fine Arts in Film Production/Cinema Studies at the New York Institute of Technology.
Sapaskis ran for New York State Senate in 2010, losing to Adriano Espaillat.
Sapaskis ran for NY-15 in 2022, losing to Ritchie Torres 82.7%–17.2%.
Sapaskis ran for New York City Council District 11 in 2025, losing to incumbent Eric Dinowitz.

priorities.text: "Under the current Democratic influences and policies, our country is suffering inflation and the raising of gas and food prices."
"As your Congressman, I purpose to elevate minimum wage to 20 dollars per hour as well as having financial aid to be offered in higher education."

positions.summary: Sapaskis says he would raise the minimum wage to $20 an hour.
positions.quote: As your Congressman, I purpose to elevate minimum wage to 20 dollars per hour as well as having financial aid to be offered in higher education.

positions.summary: Sapaskis calls for more police presence, along with addressing affordability and employment for people with disabilities.
positions.quote: The Democratic Party does not address the needs of affordable living, more police presence and employment for the disabled.

candidates.researchNotes: No dedicated 2026 campaign website was located; positions above come from a candidate questionnaire response published by iVoterGuide. Sapaskis has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey.

candidates.name: Gonzalo Duran
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed after the Conservative Party primary was canceled

summary.text: Duran is a Bronx-born former U.S. Marine and CEO running on the Conservative Party line, with vice chairmanship of the Bronx Conservative Party. His campaign centers on opposing what he calls socialism, along with public safety, housing development pressure, and government transparency in the Bronx.

background.text: Duran was born in New York, New York, and served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 2003 to 2011.
Duran earned a high school diploma from DeWitt Clinton High School and a bachelor's degree from Fordham University in 2014.
Duran works as CEO of Devil Dog USA Inc. and as Editor-in-Chief of the Big Apple Gazette.
Duran serves as Vice Chairman of the Bronx Conservative Party and as a district leader for the 79th Assembly District.
Duran previously ran for NY-15 in 2024 (on the Republican and Conservative lines, losing to Torres) and for New York City Public Advocate and Mayor in 2025.

priorities.text: "My top priority in this race is to confront and push back against socialism."
"I have long advocated for veterans, family values, community stability, and quality of life."
"Government transparency is lacking, and residents are rightfully asking where their money is going."

positions.summary: Duran's campaign platform calls for more NYPD officers and foot patrols in high-crime areas alongside community outreach.
positions.quote: Increase the amount of NYPD and surveillance to areas with high crime rates.

positions.summary: Duran's platform calls for stronger regulation of developers and legislation to prevent large rent increases.
positions.quote: Encourage landlords to cap rent at an affordable level. Build stronger legislation to protect residents from landlords who drastically raise the rent.

candidates.researchNotes: Some platform-page material (police/housing positions) appears to originate from Duran's earlier City Council campaign but remains posted on his current 2026 campaign site. Duran has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey.

summary.text: Easton is a lifelong Bronx resident and public-school teacher running on the Party for Socialism and Liberation line. He completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, describing a platform built around public housing, a $30 minimum wage, and ending U.S. military aid to Israel.

background.text: "I am an educator, father, husband, and socialist, running for Congress to represent New York's 15th Congressional District. I am a lifelong Bronx resident and have taught in South Bronx public schools for 13 years."

priorities.text: "My campaign is building a grassroots movement in the Bronx for socialism. The Bronx deserves lower rent, higher wages, clean air, free healthcare, fully funded schools, and a future that belongs to us — not the billionaires, not the landlords, but the workers who make society run."

"I will fight to repeal the Faircloth Amendment, the federal ban that's blocked new public housing construction for decades. New public housing builds will not only be good quality and fully modernized, but also truly affordable, with rents that cost us no more than 20% of our income."
"That's why, on day one, I will fight to raise the federal minimum wage to $30 an hour."
"In Congress, I will demand the bloated U.S. military budget be slashed by 90%. I will also fight to end all U.S. aid to Israel."

positions.summary: Easton calls for repealing the federal Faircloth Amendment so new public housing can be built.
positions.quote: I will fight to repeal the Faircloth Amendment, the federal ban that's blocked new public housing construction for decades.

positions.summary: Easton says new public housing should be capped at 20% of a resident's income and that housing should be removed from the private profit motive.
positions.quote: New public housing builds will not only be good quality and fully modernized, but also truly affordable, with rents that cost us no more than 20% of our income.

positions.summary: Easton would raise the federal minimum wage to $30 an hour.
positions.quote: That's why, on day one, I will fight to raise the federal minimum wage to $30 an hour.

positions.summary: Easton says he would end all U.S. military aid to Israel and cut military spending broadly.
positions.quote: I will demand the bloated U.S. military budget be slashed by 90%. I will also fight to end all U.S. aid to Israel.

candidates.name: Jose Vega
candidates.ballotNote: Lost the June 23 Democratic primary to Torres (22.2%); on the November general-election ballot on the Speak The Truth Party line

summary.text: Vega is a Bronx-born political organizer affiliated with the LaRouche movement who ran unsuccessfully in the 2026 Democratic primary and appears on the general-election ballot on the Speak The Truth Party line. His platform centers on Medicare for All, reindustrializing the Bronx, immigration reform, and ending U.S. involvement in foreign wars.

background.text: Vega is a political organizer from the South Bronx who has worked with the LaRouche movement since age 16, organizing educational programs in science and philosophy.
Vega previously ran for NY-15 in 2024, appearing on the ballot on the LaRouche Party line and receiving 2.4% of the vote; his campaign describes that run as an independent candidacy.

priorities.text: "Make the Bronx the center for reindustrialization of the United States"

positions.summary: Vega's platform calls for 'a real medicare for all policy.'
positions.quote: A real medicare for all policy

positions.summary: Vega opposes deporting long-settled immigrants and proposes residency pathways and temporary work visas instead.
positions.quote: Millions of immigrants, who have lived in this nation for perhaps as long as 50 years, are now being threatened with forced deportation

positions.summary: In a statement titled 'Reject AIPAC, and Reject War,' Vega's campaign cited calls, including from Israeli citizens, for American funding of Israel's military campaign to stop until the war ends.
positions.quote: students, young people, and even strong supporters of Israel, including Israeli citizens, have called for the war to stop, and for American funding of Israel to stop, until the war stops.
